## codegraph
# Codegraph — code intelligence over an indexed knowledge graph

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol, edge, and file in
the workspace — pre-computed structure you would otherwise re-derive by
reading files (cached intelligence: thousands of parse/trace decisions you
don't pay to re-reason each run). Reads are sub-millisecond; the index lags
writes by ~1s through the file watcher. Reach for it BEFORE *and* while
writing or editing code — not just for questions: one call returns the
verbatim source PLUS who calls it and what it affects, so you edit with the
blast radius in view. More accurate context, in far fewer tokens and
round-trips than reading files yourself.

## One tool: codegraph_explore — use it instead of reading files

There is a single tool, `codegraph_explore`, and it is Read-equivalent. It
takes either a natural-language question or a bag of symbol/file names and
returns the **verbatim, line-numbered source** of the relevant symbols
grouped by file — the same `<n>\t<line>` shape `Read` gives you, safe to
`Edit` from — PLUS the call path among them (including dynamic-dispatch hops
like callbacks, React re-render, and JSX children that grep can't follow) and
a blast-radius summary of what depends on them.

Whether you're answering "how does X work" or implementing a change (fixing a
bug, adding a feature), call `codegraph_explore` before you Read. ONE call
usually answers the whole question. Codegraph IS the pre-built search index —
so running your own grep + read loop, or delegating the lookup to a separate
file-reading sub-task/agent, repeats work codegraph already did and costs more
for the same answer. A direct codegraph answer is typically one to a few
calls; a grep/read exploration is dozens.

## How to query

- **Almost any question — "how does X work", architecture, a bug, "what/where is X", or surveying an area** → `codegraph_explore` with a natural-language question or the relevant names. ONE capped call returns the verbatim source grouped by file; most often the ONLY call y… [truncated]

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. **`s3presign.Runner` — every 12 hours (plus one immediate `RunOnce` at startup) — `server/server.go:162-171` (called from `Start` at `server/server.go:129`)**

Details:

- **Component**: `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go` — `Runner` (`NewRunner`, `Run`, `RunOnce`, `CheckAndPresign`). It pages through S3-backed attachments (`StorageType = AttachmentStorageType_S3`, batches of 100), re-presigns each object's GET URL via `s3.NewClient(...).PresignGetObject`, and writes the new URL back as the attachment's `Reference` along with `LastPresignedTime` (`store/attachment.go` `UpdateAttachment`).
- **Schedule**: `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`); `Run` ticks on that interval until its context is cancelled (`runner.go:29-41`). Within each pass, an attachment is skipped if its presigned URL is still valid for the next 4 days — the URLs are issued with a 5-day expiry (`runner.go:85-91`).
- **Wiring**: `Server.startBackgroundRunners` (`server/server.go:153`) creates the runner at `server/server.go:162`, runs it once synchronously at `server/server.go:163`, then launches the ticker loop in a goroutine at `server/server.go:167-171` under a dedicated cancellable context whose cancel func is registered for shutdown (`server/server.go:156-159`). `startBackgroundRunners` is invoked from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`.

content.text:
h02.

**`webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (the actual `safeClient.Do(req)` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`); SSRF guard = `safeDialContext` reserved-IP check at dial time — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`, backed by `isReservedIP`/`reservedCIDRs` in `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-54`**

How it fits together:

- **Trigger → delivery**: memo changes call the dispatch helpers in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` (e.g. `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`, `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook`), which call `webhook.PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`). That only enqueues onto a bounded 128-slot channel (`webhook.go:39`, drops with a warning when full); four worker goroutines started in `init` (`webhook.go:42-55`) pop the queue and call `Post`. So `Post` is where the outbound HTTP request is built, HMAC-signed (Standard Webhooks `webhook-id`/`webhook-timestamp`/`webhook-signature` headers), and executed.
- **Primary protection (dial time)**: all dispatches go through the shared `safeClient` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`) whose `Transport.DialContext` is `safeDialContext`. It splits host/port, resolves the host itself, and refuses to dial if *any* resolved address falls in a reserved range. Because the check happens at connect time on the addresses actually resolved, it also defeats DNS rebinding and redirect-to-internal — noted in the comment at `webhook.go:30-31`.
- **Secondary protection (config time)**: `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`) rejects non-http(s) schemes and hostnames resolving to reserved IPs when a webhook is created or updated — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74` and `:161`/`:182`.
- **Blocked ranges**: loopback, RFC-1918, link-local incl. cloud IMDS `169.254.169.254`, plus IPv6 `::1/128`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`), parsed once in `init` (`validate.go:28-36`).
- **Escape hatch**: the package-level `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` flag (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`) short-circuits `isReservedIP`, disabling both layers for self-hosted setups. Note it is declared but never assigned anywhere in non-test code — no CLI flag or env var currently sets it, so it stays `false` in practice.

**`internal/idp` (package `idp`, `internal/idp/idp.go`); `internal/idp/oauth2` (package `oauth2`, `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`) — OAuth2 is the only concrete protocol implementation that ships**

Details:

- **Abstraction package**: `internal/idp` — `internal/idp/idp.go:3` defines the shared `IdentityProviderUserInfo` struct (`Identifier`, `DisplayName`, `Email`, `AvatarURL`) that every provider must produce. Note the abstraction is thin: it's a common result type, not a Go interface — there is no `IdentityProvider` interface in the package.
- **Implementation package**: `internal/idp/oauth2` — `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` provides `IdentityProvider` (line 20), `NewIdentityProvider` (line 27, validates `clientId`/`clientSecret`/`tokenUrl`/`userInfoUrl`/`fieldMapping.identifier`), `ExchangeToken` (line 47, with PKCE `code_verifier` support), and `UserInfo` (line 83, maps provider claims into `idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo` via the configured field mapping).
- **Corroborating evidence that OAuth2 is the only one**: the provider type enum has exactly one non-unspecified value, `OAUTH2 = 1` (`proto/gen/api/v1/idp_service.pb.go` `IdentityProvider_Type`; `proto/gen/store/idp.pb.go`), and `IdentityProviderConfig` is a oneof with a single `oauth2_config` member. `internal/idp/` contains only `idp.go` and the `oauth2/` subdirectory.
- **Call site**: `resolveSSOIdentity` in `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go` constructs the OAuth2 provider and calls `ExchangeToken` then `UserInfo`.

func NewDBDriver(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
	var driver store.Driver
	var err error

	switch profile.Driver {
	case "sqlite":
		driver, err = sqlite.NewDB(profile)
	case "mysql":
		driver, err = mysql.NewDB(profile)
	case "postgres":
		driver, err = postgres.NewDB(profile)
	default:
		return nil, errors.New("unknown db driver")

	if err != nil {
		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create db driver")

}

h05.

**Explicit Go code — two `DELETE FROM reaction` statements inside the per-driver `DeleteUser` transaction, in all three drivers. There is no database-level cascade for reactions.**

Evidence locations:

**1. The Go code that does it.** `Store.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:171`) delegates to `s.driver.DeleteUser`, and each driver's `deleteUserTargetsTx` runs two reaction deletes before removing the user row:

- `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go` — `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` called at lines 93 and 102 of `deleteUserTargetsTx`; implementations at `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (`DELETE FROM reaction WHERE content_id IN (...)`, batched at 500) and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (`DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = ?`).
- `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96` and `:102` (implementations at `:417` and `:437`).
- `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96` and `:102` (implementations at `:380` and `:400`).

The two deletes cover different things: *by content ID* removes everyone's reactions on the deleted user's memos (content IDs built as `"memos/"+memo.UID` by `memoContentIDsFromRefs`, over the recursive memo+comment tree); *by creator ID* removes the deleted user's own reactions on other people's memos. All of it runs inside the single `BeginTx`/`Commit` in `DeleteUser`.

**2. The schema, showing no DB-level rule.** The `reaction` table has no foreign key and no `ON DELETE CASCADE` in any dialect:

- `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`
- `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98`
- `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`

Each declares only `id`, `created_ts`, `creator_id`, `content_id`, `reaction_type` plus a `UNIQUE(creator_id, content_id, reaction_type)` — `creator_id` is a plain `INTEGER NOT NULL`, not a reference to `user(id)`. Grepping `REFERENCES|CASCADE` across `store/migration/` returns cascades only for `memo_share`, `memo_resource`, `user_setting`, etc., never for `reaction`. (Note `content_id` is a text resource name like `memos/<uid>`, not an integer FK, so a cascade from `memo` isn't even expressible here.)

**3. Test confirmation.** `server/router/api/v1/test/user_service_delete_test.go` seeds reactions on the user's own memo, on their comment on a foreign memo, and a peer's reaction on a foreign memo (lines 188-209), then after deletion asserts the first two sets are empty and the unrelated peer reaction survives (lines 287-298).

h06.

**Handlers: `CreateMemo`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`, `CreateMemoComment`, `SetMemoAttachments`, `SetMemoRelations` — all in `server/router/api/v1/`; convergence: `webhook.PostAsync` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:184` (which hands off to the actual delivery function `webhook.Post`, `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`)**

The user-configured URL is a per-user webhook URL stored via `CreateUserWebhook`/`UpdateUserWebhook` and read back by `s.Store.GetUserWebhooks`.

Paths:

| RPC handler | route to dispatch |
|---|---|
| `CreateMemo` — `memo_service.go:70` | `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` at `memo_service.go:157` |
| `UpdateMemo` — `memo_service.go:401` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `memo_service.go:513` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` at `memo_update_helpers.go:67` |
| `DeleteMemo` — `memo_service.go:518` | `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` at `memo_service.go:562` |
| `CreateMemoComment` — `memo_service_comments.go:20` | `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` at `memo_service_comments.go:119` |
| `SetMemoAttachments` — `memo_attachment_service.go:16` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `memo_attachment_service.go:48` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` |
| `SetMemoRelations` — `memo_relation_service.go:16` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `memo_relation_service.go:48` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` |

All four `Dispatch*Webhook` methods live in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`. The three memo-lifecycle ones funnel through the unexported `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (`memo_service_webhooks.go:47`); the comment one has its own loop (`:30`) because it targets the *related* memo owner's webhooks rather than the actor's. Both loops end at the same call: `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` (`memo_service_webhooks.go:41` and `:70`).

`PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`) is therefore the single function every handler path converges on. It only enqueues onto a bounded 128-slot channel (`webhook.go:39`), dropping with a warning if full; four worker goroutines started in `init` (`webhook.go:42-55`) dequeue and call `Post` (`webhook.go:120`), which builds the signed request and executes it via `safeClient.Do` (`webhook.go:152`). So if you want the function that performs delivery itself rather than the last shared caller before it, that's `Post`.

h07.

The browser hits `GET /file/users/{username}/avatar` (the URL the API hands out in `user_service_converters.go:36`, `fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name)` where `Name` is `users/{username}`). Hops:

```
RegisterRoutes (route: GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121,124
serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168
getCurrentUser → authenticator.AuthenticateToUser — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708 (server/auth)
getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148
Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:136
Driver.ListUsers (interface dispatch) — store/driver.go
DB.ListUsers (per-driver SQL, e.g. SELECT ... FROM user WHERE username = ?) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (also store/db/mysql/user.go, store/db/postgres/user.go)
parseDataURI (decode stored data URI to bytes) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737
c.Blob (respond with image bytes) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:209
```

Notes on the path:

- **Wiring**: the file server is constructed and mounted at server startup — `fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)` then `RegisterRoutes(echoServer)` at `server/server.go:81-82`. This is a plain Echo route, not a gRPC/Connect RPC — there is no `GetUserAvatar` RPC.
- **Access control** (`fileserver.go:173-181`): if the instance is not anonymous-accessible (`s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()` false), the request must authenticate via `getCurrentUser` → `auth.Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` (Bearer access token / PAT, or refresh-token cookie). Otherwise any visitor may fetch any user's avatar.
- **Where the data actually lives**: the avatar is *not* an attachment or a file on disk — it's stored inline on the user row as a base64 `data:` URI in `user.avatar_url` (`store.User.AvatarURL`, `store/user.go:29`). `serveUserAvatar` reads it off the user record, decodes it with `parseDataURI` (`fileserver.go:737`, regex at `fileserver.go:98`), rejects MIME types outside `avatarAllowedTypes` (`fileserver.go:75-83`, checked at `:201`), sets security + cache headers (`setSecurityHeaders` at `:758`, `cacheMaxAge` 1 hour), and writes the bytes.
- **Cache layer**: `Store.GetUser` only consults `userCache` when looking up by ID; this lookup is by username (`FindUser{Username: &identifier}`), so it always falls through to `Store.ListUsers` → the driver, and the result is then cached by ID (`store/user.go:143`).

106		} else {

110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {

113		}

154		// Create a separate context for each background runner

**`(*Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — ~38 call sites (~37 distinct calling functions: 30 test functions + 7 production sites)**

How I measured: I enumerated every `func` declared under `internal/` (370 distinct names, excluding `_test.go` declarations), counted `name(` occurrences repo-wide minus declarations, then hand-disambiguated the top of the list to drop names that collide across packages (`Error`, `New`, `Len`, `Next`, `contains`, `Field`, `Stop`, …). `CompileToStatement` is unambiguous — the string `.CompileToStatement(` appears 38 times in the repo and there is exactly one declaration.

Distribution of the 38 call sites:

- `internal/filter/functions_test.go` — 17 (16 distinct test funcs)
- `internal/filter/engine_test.go` — 8 (8 distinct test funcs)
- `internal/filter/time_test.go` — 6 (6 distinct test funcs)
- `internal/filter/helpers.go:11` — 1, inside `AppendConditions`, which is itself called from 6 places (`store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/memo.go` and `.../attachment.go`) — so this one site carries most of the real production traffic
- `store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go` — 2; `store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go` — 1; `store/db/mysql/memo_relation.go` — 1
- `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go` — 1; `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go` — 1

Runners-up, for calibration (same counting method): `filter.NewEngine` (`internal/filter/engine.go:24`) ≈ 32 sites, `filter.NewSchema` (`internal/filter/schema.go:89`) ≈ 29, `(*renderer).addArg` (`internal/filter/render.go:842`) 28 — all 28 inside `internal/filter/render.go` — and `util.GenUUID` (`internal/util/util.go:40`) 28.

Caveat worth stating: if you count *production-only* fan-in, the ranking changes completely — `CompileToStatement` has only 7 non-test call sites, while `(*renderer).addArg` has all 28 of its calls in production code, making `addArg` the highest-fan-in internal symbol under that definition. The codegraph index's own "N callers" figures were not usable here (e.g. it reported "115 callers in server/server.go" for `s3presign.Run`), so these numbers come from direct grep.

**`(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (the INSERT is built at line 41 and executed by `d.db.QueryRowContext` at line 42); determined by resolving the `store.Driver` interface dispatch back to the concrete type chosen by the startup driver switch under default config.**

The runtime path:

1. `CreateMemo` RPC → `s.Store.CreateMemo(ctx, create)` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:115`
2. `Store.CreateMemo` validates the UID then delegates: `return s.driver.CreateMemo(ctx, create)` — `store/memo.go:109-114`
3. `s.driver` is the interface field `driver Driver` (`store/store.go:15`, interface at `store/driver.go`), so the concrete method is not statically visible here — three types implement it: `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16`, `store/db/mysql/memo.go`, `store/db/postgres/memo.go`.
4. The concrete type is fixed at startup: `db.NewDBDriver(instanceProfile)` — `cmd/memos/main.go:57` — whose `switch profile.Driver` picks `sqlite.NewDB(profile)` at `store/db/db.go:19-20`; the result is handed to `store.New(dbDriver, instanceProfile)` at `cmd/memos/main.go:64` and stored as `driver` (`store/store.go:47-49`).
5. With no flags, `profile.Driver` is `"sqlite"` — `viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")` at `cmd/memos/main.go:122`, matching the flag default at `:130`. So `NewDB` returns `*sqlite.DB` (`store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:24`), and `s.driver.CreateMemo` binds to `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo`.

The statement it runs (`store/db/sqlite/memo.go:41`):

```sql
INSERT INTO `memo` (`uid`, `creator_id`, `content`, `visibility`, `payload` [, `created_ts`, `updated_ts`])
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ? [, ?, ?])
RETURNING `id`, `created_ts`, `updated_ts`, `row_status`
```

**How I determined it among the three candidates** — not by picking the "obvious" one, but by following the configuration that binds the interface:

- Located the single assignment of the interface field (`store.New`, `store/store.go:38-61`) and its only production caller (`cmd/memos/main.go:64`).
- Traced its argument to the one factory that constructs drivers, `db.NewDBDriver` (`store/db/db.go:14`), and read its `switch` — the sole selection point (confirmed earlier: the `store/db/mysql` and `store/db/postgres` packages are imported nowhere else).
- Resolved `profile.Driver` for a default install: viper default `"sqlite"` (`cmd/memos/main.go:122`), cobra flag default `"sqlite"` (`:130`), bound at `:151`. Nothing else writes `Driver`. Corroborating: `profile.Validate` only synthesizes a DSN in the `p.Driver == "sqlite"` branch — `<data>/memos_prod.db` (`internal/profile/profile.go:110-117`) — which is what makes a flag-less install work at all; `mysql.NewDB`/`postgres.NewDB` would fail on the empty DSN.

One correction to my earlier h02 answer: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` **is** wired to a real flag — `--allow-private-webhooks` (default `false`), declared at `cmd/memos/main.go:133`, bound at `:160`, assigned at `cmd/memos/main.go:49`. My earlier grep missed it because the shell's recursive `grep` honors `.gitignore`, which lists `memos` as a build artifact and so silently skips the `cmd/memos/` directory. Everything else in the previous answers is unaffected — I re-checked `cmd/memos/` directly for `mysql`, `RunOnce`, `.Close()`, `GenUUID`, `CompileToStatement`, and `store.User`/`Memo`/`Attachment` references, and it has none.

h13.

**Impl: exactly one — the unexported `*markdown.service` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:58`); Construction: `markdown.NewService(...)` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:85`), called in production from `NewAPIV1Service` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48`); Holders: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`), `RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`), and `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`, dead) — plus the free function `RebuildMemoPayload`, which takes the interface as a parameter (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`)**

Details:

**The interface** — `markdown.Service` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`) declares eight methods: `ExtractAll`, `ExtractTags`, `ExtractProperties`, `RenderMarkdown`, `RenderHTML`, `GenerateSnippet`, `ValidateContent`, `RenameTag`.

**The single implementation** — `type service struct { md goldmark.Markdown }` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:58`). All eight methods are declared on `*service` (`markdown.go:143, 193, 244, 255, 264, 349, 356, 425`, plus the private `parse` at `:116`). There is no second implementation anywhere — no mock, fake, or alternate backend; searching for `markdown.Service` outside the package yields only holder fields and parameters, never another type. (`internal/markdown/renderer.MarkdownRenderer` is a goldmark AST-to-markdown renderer used *inside* `RenderMarkdown` at `markdown.go:250`, not an implementation of `Service`.)

**Construction** — `NewService(opts ...Option) Service` (`markdown.go:85`) builds a goldmark instance with GFM plus optionally the repo's own `TagExtension`/`MentionExtension` (`internal/markdown/extensions/`), and returns `&service{md: md}`. The one production call site is `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48`, with both `markdown.WithTagExtension()` and `markdown.WithMentionExtension()` enabled; it's invoked from `server.NewServer` via `apiv1.NewAPIV1Service` (`server/server.go:76`). Test-only constructions exist at `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:427`, and `server/router/rss/rss_test.go:54` (the last with no options, so tags/mentions off).

**Holders and propagation** — the single instance is shared: `APIV1Service` holds it and hands the same value to the RSS service at `server/server.go:85` (`rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService)`). Consumers: `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32`), `GenerateSnippet` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:85`), `RenderHTML` for feeds (`server/router/rss/rss.go:339`), and `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService)` on memo create/update (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`, `:447`).

The `memopayload.Runner` holder is worth flagging: nothing constructs it in production (`memopayload.NewRunner` has no non-test callers), so that field never holds a live value — only the package's free function `RebuildMemoPayload` is actually used.

h14.

**Computation site: `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`, delegating to `markdown.Service.ExtractAll` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`. Triggers: memo create and content-update. Extracted: `tags` plus the `Property` set — `title`, `has_link`, `has_code`, `has_task_list`, `has_incomplete_tasks`.**

**Where it's computed.** `RebuildMemoPayload(_ ctx, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service)` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74-87`) initializes `memo.Payload` if nil, calls `markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))`, and assigns the two derived fields:

```go
memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
```

(`runner.go:85-86` — the only place in the codebase that writes either field.) The actual work is a single goldmark AST walk in `(*service).ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:356-422`). The payload is persisted as protojson in the memo row's `payload` column (e.g. `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:17-27`).

**Triggers.** Only two production call sites, both in the memo RPC layer:

- `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`, run on the `store.Memo` before `s.Store.CreateMemo`.
- `UpdateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`, inside the `if path == "content"` branch of the update-mask loop, so recomputation happens **only** when `content` is in the field mask; the fresh payload is then assigned to `update.Payload` (`:450`). Updates to visibility, pinned, etc. do not recompute.

A third caller exists but is dead: `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52`) would rebuild every memo in 100-row batches, but nothing constructs `memopayload.NewRunner` outside the package — unlike the s3presign runner, it is not wired into `startBackgroundRunners` (`server/server.go:153`). So there is no backfill path in a running server.

**What's extracted** (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:362-421`):

- `Tags` — text of every `mast.TagNode` (`#tag`), skipping tags nested inside links/images (`asMemoTagNode`, `markdown.go:130`), deduplicated case-preservingly.
- `Property.Title` — text of the first block-level child of the document if it is an H1 heading (`markdown.go:383-389`).
- `Property.HasLink` — any `gast.KindLink` node.
- `Property.HasCode` — any code block, fenced code block, or code span.
- `Property.HasTaskList` — any `east.KindTaskCheckBox`; and `Property.HasIncompleteTasks` when such a checkbox is unchecked.

The proto shape is `MemoPayload.Property` in `proto/store/memo.proto:15-22` (`has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title`), with `tags` as `MemoPayload.tags` (`:12`).

`ExtractAll` also collects `Mentions`, but `RebuildMemoPayload` does not store them — mentions are consumed separately at read/notify time via `s.MarkdownService.ExtractAll` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32`.

**Consumers** (why it exists): `convertMemoFromStore` copies `Payload.Tags` and `Payload.Property` onto the API `Memo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:48-49`), and user stats aggregate them (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:138-148`). Note the list/preview *snippet* is a different thing — it is computed on read, not stored, via `getMemoContentSnippet` → `MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(content, 64)` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83-88`, used at `memo_service_converter.go:76` and `:225`).

h15.

Enforcement sites, grouped by server surface:

```
checkMemoReadAccess (per-memo gate for GetMemo, its parent memo, and ListMemoComments) — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39 (callers :356, :367, server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:148)
ListMemos visibility scoping (VisibilityList / CEL filter injection) — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:213-227
ListMemoReactions visibility gate — server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30-41
UpsertMemoReaction / DeleteMemoReaction private-memo gate — server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:83 (and the same check in DeleteMemoReaction, :111+)
CreateMemoComment private-parent gate — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41
ListMemoAttachments visibility gate — server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:213-225
checkAttachmentAccess (attachment inherits its memo's visibility) — server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:422 (visibility branch at :445-452)
User stats visibility scoping (GetUserStats / ListAllUserStats) — server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84-90 and :218-220
canViewerAccessMemo (redacts memo snippet in notifications) — server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:302
Mention-notification eligibility (skips private/foreign memos) — server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:62-84
SSEClient.canReceive (per-subscriber event fan-out filter) — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134
checkAttachmentPermission (raw file serving, incl. anonymous-instance rule) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650 (visibility branches at :677, :699)
canViewerAccessMemo (email notification body redaction) — server/notification/email.go:306
RSS feeds — public-only query — server/router/rss/rss.go:90 (instance feed) and :141 (per-user feed)
Sitemap generation — public-only query — server/router/frontend/frontend.go:149-151
```

Two things worth calling out:

- **The rules are re-implemented, not shared.** The API layer's shape is "`!= Public` → require auth; `== Private` → require creator or super-user" (`memo_service.go:55-66`), but `fileserver.checkAttachmentPermission` uses `user.Role != store.RoleAdmin` directly instead of `isSuperUser`, and additionally gates public memos on `s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()` (`fileserver.go:677`). `canViewerAccessMemo` exists twice with slightly different admin checks — `isSuperUser(viewer)` in `user_service_notifications.go:305` vs. `viewer.Role == store.RoleAdmin` in `notification/email.go:309`.
- **Two deliberate bypasses.** Share tokens skip visibility entirely: `GetMemoByShare` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go:153`) authorizes on an unexpired `MemoShare` and never consults `memo.Visibility` (it only rejects archived/missing memos), and `fileserver.go:684-689` accepts a `?share_token=` query param for attachments on private/protected memos.

**Premise correction: there is no Redis anywhere in this repository.** The word "redis" does not appear in any `.go`, `.mod`, `.sum`, `.yaml`, or frontend source file, and `go.mod` lists no Redis client (no `go-redis`, `redigo`, or similar). The cache layer is a hand-rolled, in-process, in-memory cache — nothing is configured, connected, or persisted externally, and cached data does not survive a restart or get shared between instances.

**Actual mechanism:**

- **Implementation**: `store/cache/cache.go` — a `Cache` struct backed by a `sync.Map` plus an atomic item counter (`store/cache/cache.go:67-73`), satisfying the local `Interface` (`cache.go:11-32`). Entries are `item{value, expiration, size}` (`cache.go:35-39`); expiry is enforced lazily on read (`Get` deletes and reports a miss if `time.Now().After(itm.expiration)`, `cache.go:132-146`) and by a background cleanup goroutine, with `cleanupOldest` evicting when `MaxItems` is exceeded (`cache.go:117-119`).
- **Where it's configured**: `store.New` in `store/store.go:38-61`. The `cache.Config` literal there is the only configuration point — there is no flag, env var, or config file for it:

```go
cacheConfig := cache.Config{
    DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
    CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
    MaxItems:        1000,
    OnEviction:      nil,
}
```

  Three caches are built from that same config: `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (`store/store.go:51-53`). Note `cache.DefaultConfig()` (`cache.go:57-64`) declares identical values but is not what `store.New` uses.

- **TTL for user entries: 10 minutes.** Every user write goes through `Set`, not `SetWithTTL` — `store/user.go:98`, `:122`, `:132`, `:143`, `:167` — and `Set` applies `c.config.DefaultTTL` (`store/cache/cache.go:93-95`), i.e. the 10 minutes from `store/store.go:41`. No call site anywhere passes a custom TTL for users.
- **Keying and invalidation**: the key is just the decimal user ID (`userCacheKey`, `store/user.go:88-90`) — so lookups only hit the cache when finding by ID (`Store.GetUser`, `store/user.go:149-156`); username/email lookups always fall through to the driver. Entries are explicitly evicted on user deletion (`store/user_delete.go:40`), and all three caches are shut down in `Store.Close` (`store/store.go:74-76`).

There is one other, unrelated cache in the backend: a small in-process RSS response cache in `server/router/rss/rss.go` (`cacheEntry` at `:35`, `putInCache`) — also memory-only, also not Redis.

r02.

**Premise correction: there is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware in this repository. No rate limiter is registered anywhere, and no request limits exist to report.**

Evidence:

- A case-insensitive search of all Go sources for `ratelimit`, `rate_limit`, `rate limit`, `throttl`, `RateLimiter`, and the usual token-bucket dependency `golang.org/x/time/rate` returns exactly one hit, and it's a comment describing future work, not code: `internal/email/doc.go:86` — `//   - Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse`. `go.mod` pulls in no rate-limiting library.
- The complete global middleware stack is two entries, registered in `server.NewServer`: `middleware.Recover()` (`server/server.go:51`) and `newCORSMiddleware(profile)` (`server/server.go:52`, defined in `server/cors.go:14`). Echo's `middleware.RateLimiter`/`RateLimiterWithConfig` is never used; the only other `middleware.` reference is `middleware.StaticWithConfig` for serving frontend assets (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go:54`).
- The API interceptor chain has no limiter either: the Connect handlers are wired with `NewMetadataInterceptor`, `NewLoggingInterceptor`, `NewRecoveryInterceptor`, and `NewAuthInterceptor` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-137`), and the gRPC-Gateway path gets the same shared authorizer as auth middleware (`v1.go:67`, `:95`).

What does exist — related but not rate limiting, in case one of these is what you were after:

- **Request body size cap**: `connect.WithReadMaxBytes(maxAPIRequestBytes)` on the Connect mux (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:141`) — a per-request byte ceiling, not a per-user request-frequency limit.
- **Concurrency semaphores**: thumbnail generation is capped at 3 concurrent operations (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:46`, `:116`), and `APIV1Service` holds `thumbnailSemaphore` (3) and `imageProcessingSemaphore` (2) (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:63-64`). These bound in-flight work process-wide; they don't track or limit anything per user.
- **Content/upload size limits**: memo content length (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:101-106`) and attachment upload size (`server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:120-124`), both instance settings.
- **Webhook queue backpressure**: the async dispatch channel holds 128 items and drops with a warning when full (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`, `:189-195`) — a queue bound, not a limiter.

So an abusive authenticated client is bounded only by these size and concurrency caps; nothing restricts how many API calls a given user may make per unit time.

**Premise correction: there is no nightly database-cleanup job, and the cron scheduler is never started by the server — so there is no scheduled time to report.**

Two separate premise failures:

**1. No database-cleanup job exists.** Nothing in the codebase registers any job that vacuums, purges, prunes, or otherwise cleans the database on a schedule. Searching non-test Go code for `cleanup|vacuum|purge|prune` turns up only unrelated things: per-request attachment-storage cleanup during user deletion (`server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:421-450`, `store/attachment.go:171`), a best-effort rollback of a provisional SSO user row (`server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:76`), and the in-memory cache's `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute` (`store/store.go:42`) — which expires cache entries in RAM, not database rows.

**2. `internal/scheduler` is dead code — nothing in the running server uses it.** The package is fully built out (`job.go`, `parser.go` with a 5/6-field cron parser and IANA timezone support, `scheduler.go`, `middleware.go`, plus a README and `doc.go`), but the only files that import `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler` are its own tests: `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13` and `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10`. No production file references `scheduler.New`, `Scheduler.Register`, or `Scheduler.Start`.

Every cron expression in the repo is in a test or a doc comment — e.g. `"0 2 * * *"` appears as `// 2 AM daily` in `internal/scheduler/doc.go:16` and in `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:100`, and `"0 0 * * *" (daily at midnight)` is an example in the `Job.Schedule` field comment (`internal/scheduler/job.go:21`). These are illustrations of the API, not registered jobs. If a stale answer cites 2 AM, that's this doc comment being mistaken for configuration.

**What background work the server actually runs.** Exactly one runner, and it's interval-based rather than cron-based: `s3presign.Runner`, which re-presigns S3 attachment URLs every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`) plus one immediate pass at startup. It is wired in `Server.startBackgroundRunners` at `server/server.go:162-171`, called from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`. A second runner package, `server/runner/memopayload`, exists but is likewise never constructed in production.

r04.

**Premise correction: neither. There is no message broker in this repository at all — no NATS, no RabbitMQ, no Kafka, no AMQP client. A case-insensitive search of all Go sources and `go.mod` for `nats`, `rabbitmq`, `amqp`, `kafka`, `streadway`, and `pubsub` returns zero hits. There is no queue declaration to point to, because there is no external queue.**

**Actual mechanism — an in-process buffered Go channel with a fixed worker pool, all in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`:**

- **The "queue"** is a package-level Go channel with a hard capacity of 128:
  `var asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`. It lives in the server process's memory; nothing is persisted, so anything still queued at shutdown is silently lost, and it is not shared across replicas.
- **The workers** are 4 goroutines started in the package's `init()` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`. Each loops `for payload := range asyncPostQueue` and calls `Post(payload)`, logging a warning on failure. They are started by package initialization rather than wired into `Server.Start`, and there is no shutdown path that drains or stops them.
- **The producer** is `PostAsync` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:184-196`. It does a non-blocking `select` send: if the channel is full, the `default` branch drops the delivery and logs `"Dropped webhook dispatch because the async queue is full"` (`:191-195`). So overflow is discarded, not spooled — there is no persistence, no retry, no dead-letter, and no redelivery of any kind.
- **Delivery itself** happens in `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`, which marshals the payload, adds Standard Webhooks HMAC headers when a signing secret is set, and executes the request via the SSRF-guarded `safeClient` (`webhook.go:32-37`, `:152`).
- **Who enqueues**: the memo lifecycle dispatchers in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` — `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (`:70`) for created/updated/deleted, and `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (`:41`) for comments.

So the "workers consume from" relationship is real, but the thing they consume from is `asyncPostQueue`, a 128-slot in-memory channel declared at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39` — not a broker topic or queue binding.

content.text:
r05.

**Premise correction: there is no GraphQL anywhere in this repository — no schema file, no resolvers, no GraphQL server or client dependency. A case-insensitive search for "graphql" across all Go, TypeScript, JSON, `.graphql`, and `go.mod` files (excluding `node_modules`) returns zero hits. The public API is defined in Protocol Buffers and exposed as gRPC / Connect / REST-via-gateway, with a generated OpenAPI spec.**

**Actual API surface:**

- **Schema source of truth**: `.proto` files under `proto/api/v1/` — `auth_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `memo_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, plus shared `common.proto`. Eight services, ~73 RPCs total (largest: `UserService` 26, `MemoService` 20). Persistence-side messages live in `proto/store/` (`memo.proto`, `user_setting.proto`, `attachment.proto`, `idp.proto`, `inbox.proto`, `instance_setting.proto`). REST paths come from `google.api.http` annotations on each RPC (e.g. `/api/v1/{name=users/*}` for `GetUser`).
- **Codegen**: driven by buf — `proto/buf.gen.yaml` runs `protocolbuffers/go`, `grpc/go`, `connectrpc/go`, `grpc-ecosystem/gateway`, `community/google-gnostic-openapi`, and `bufbuild/es`. Output lands in `proto/gen/` (Go: `*.pb.go`, `*_grpc.pb.go`, `*.pb.gw.go`, `apiv1connect/*.connect.go`) and `web/src/types/proto/` (TypeScript for the frontend).
- **OpenAPI, not GraphQL introspection**: the generated spec is `proto/gen/openapi.yaml`, embedded into the binary via `//go:embed` in `proto/openapi_embed.go:4-5` and served through `proto.OpenAPIYAML()`.
- **Runtime wiring**: `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65`) mounts both transports on the Echo server — the grpc-gateway REST mux (handlers registered by `RegisterUserServiceHandlerServer` and siblings in `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go`) and the Connect handlers with interceptors `NewMetadataInterceptor`, `NewLoggingInterceptor`, `NewRecoveryInterceptor`, `NewAuthInterceptor` (`v1.go:133-141`). `NewAPIV1Service` is constructed at `server/server.go:76`.
- **Non-gRPC HTTP surfaces** alongside it: file serving at `/file/attachments/:uid/:filename` and `/file/users/:identifier/avatar` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS feeds (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), the frontend/static + sitemap routes (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go`), an MCP endpoint (`server/router/mcp/`, which does expose JSON Schema tool definitions — `server/router/mcp/openapi.go`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:67`).

If something referred to a "GraphQL schema", the closest real artifacts are the `.proto` definitions in `proto/api/v1/` (the actual schema) and `proto/gen/openapi.yaml` (the published API description).
